# tiny-flow

A minimal way to work: open the code and start building.

You begin implementation immediately, with nothing written up front.
Nothing is saved or handed off between steps.
One person drives the whole change from start to finish.
Tests are optional here, and are added only after the fact if at all.
The tool does one small job and gets out of the way.
You start from a blank idea, with no existing code, and it never ingests or maps an existing codebase.
It covers a single step, not the whole lifecycle.
The output is throwaway, meant to prove an idea fast, with no production hardening.
There is no collaboration, review, or handoff between people.
